title: Distilling Bidirectional Embedding Teachers into Streaming-Compatible Causal Students

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to provide streaming-compatible text embeddings (KV-cache reusable) without sacrificing the quality of bidirectional attention. Paper [5] discusses KV caches as lightweight representations for downstream tasks, achieving competitive performance despite being weaker than dedicated embeddings. Paper [7] explores KV cache reuse for long-text understanding, addressing computational costs and latency issues. Paper [10] investigates KV cache recycling to expand usable context capacity in low-parameter LLMs. Paper [11] describes KVLink, which eliminates inefficiency by precomputing KV caches for overlapping contexts. All these papers share the same objective of leveraging KV-cache mechanisms for efficient streaming-compatible embeddings or inference, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution uses a teacher-student distillation framework that trains a bidirectional teacher with GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) and distills it into a causal student by combining InfoNCE contrastive loss with MSE distillation loss. Paper [3] introduces DistilCSE, a knowledge distillation framework for contrastive sentence embeddings, combining contrastive learning and distillation. Paper [15] presents JDCEmb, which combines joint distillation and contrastive learning for embeddings in task-oriented dialogue systems. Paper [16] describes a training regimen combining model distillation techniques with task-specific contrastive loss for compact embedding models. Paper [17] introduces Distill CLIP, a meta teacher-student distillation framework for multimodal embeddings. While none explicitly mentions GG-SM, the mechanism of combining distillation with contrastive loss is substantively equivalent across these papers, making the mechanism covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation reports a 68.1% gap-closure relative to the teacher on MTEB and a 4.1x streaming speedup via KV-cache reuse. Paper [18] discusses MTEB as a benchmark for evaluating text embeddings, and Paper [24] introduces MMTEB, an expansion of MTEB. Both papers use the same benchmark family (MTEB/MMTEB) for evaluating embedding models. Paper [5] evaluates KV-derived representations for downstream tasks, and Paper [7] measures KV cache reuse efficiency for streaming inference. Paper [10] evaluates KV cache recycling for context expansion, and Paper [11] benchmarks KVLink for efficient KV cache reuse. The evaluation design (benchmark family and KV-cache reuse metrics) is covered across these papers.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of text embeddings and streaming inference. Paper [3] focuses on contrastive sentence embeddings, Paper [15] addresses embeddings in task-oriented dialogue systems, and Paper [16] targets general-purpose text embeddings. Papers [5], [7], [10], and [11] all explore KV-cache reuse for streaming inference in text-based applications. These papers collectively cover the domain of text embeddings and streaming inference, making the domain covered.

**PURPOSE: Provide streaming-compatible text embeddings (KV-cache reusable) without giving up the quality of bidirectional attention.**

The purpose is specifically to close the quality gap between causal (streaming-friendly) and bidirectional (quality-optimal) text embedding models. Paper [19] is the closest: it explicitly addresses "improving the performance of unidirectional RNN-based [models]" via distillation from bidirectional models for streaming speech recognition — same objective (causal/streaming model matching bidirectional quality) in a different modality. Paper [25] (Causal2Vec) also addresses "overcoming inherent limitations of causal attention in representation learning" for decoder-only LLMs as embedding models, which is the same gap. Paper [20] (SoulX-FlashTalk) addresses "conflict between computational load and strict latency constraints" using bidirectional distillation for streaming, but in avatar generation. Paper [23] also studies causal vs. bidirectional attention for user representation learning. Papers [19], [25], and [23] all pursue the same objective: make causal/unidirectional models match bidirectional quality for embeddings/representations. Paper [19] is the clearest match at the problem-class level.

---

**MECHANISM: Teacher-student distillation with GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) on the teacher + InfoNCE contrastive loss + MSE distillation loss on the student.**

The specific combination is: (1) gradient-guided soft masking applied to the bidirectional teacher during training, and (2) distilling into a causal student using InfoNCE + MSE. Paper [3] (DistilCSE) uses knowledge distillation for contrastive sentence embeddings combining contrastive loss with distillation. Paper [15] (JDCEmb) uses "joint distillation and contrastive learning for embeddings." Paper [16] (jina-embeddings-v5) combines "model distillation techniques with task-specific contrastive loss." Paper [19] uses KD from bidirectional to unidirectional models. However, the GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) component — using gradient signals to guide soft masking of the teacher's attention — is a specific primitive. Paper [6] uses "masked knowledge distillation" but for video modeling. Paper [4] uses "mask adaptive mechanism" for KD in medical segmentation. None of the prior papers combine gradient-guided soft masking of a bidirectional teacher with InfoNCE+MSE distillation into a causal student specifically for text embeddings. The InfoNCE+MSE combination for embedding distillation appears in [3], [15], [16], but the GG-SM teacher-side masking primitive is not present. The closest is [3]/[15]/[16] for the distillation+contrastive combination, but the gradient-guided soft masking of the teacher is absent.

---

**EVALUATION: 68.1% gap-closure on MTEB + 4.1x streaming speedup via KV-cache reuse.**

MTEB is a named benchmark family used in papers [18] and [24]. Paper [18] explicitly uses MTEB for evaluating text embedding models. Paper [24] introduces MMTEB as an expansion of MTEB. The evaluation design of measuring performance on MTEB is covered by [18]. The speedup measurement via KV-cache reuse is a standard efficiency metric seen in [5], [7], [11]. The "gap-closure" metric framing is a specific reporting choice, but the underlying design (MTEB benchmark + efficiency measurement) is covered.

---

**DOMAIN: Text embeddings / streaming inference.**

Text embeddings are directly addressed in [3] (contrastive sentence embeddings), [15] (embeddings for dialogue), [16] (text embedding distillation), [18] (general text embedding, MTEB), [24] (MTEB), [25] (decoder-only LLMs as embedding models). Streaming inference for LLMs is addressed in [5], [7], [11], [27]. The domain of text embeddings is clearly covered by multiple papers.
